questions.question: What are the main ingredients of a classic Spanish tortilla?
questions.fact: The great tortilla debate: "con cebolla" or "sin cebolla", with onion or without? Spain is still divided.

questions.question: Gazpacho is a cold soup made mainly from…
questions.fact: Gazpacho comes from Andalusia. Its thicker cousin from Córdoba, topped with egg and ham, is called salmorejo.

questions.question: Which country does sushi come from?
questions.fact: Sushi doesn't mean raw fish: it means the vinegared rice. Raw fish on its own is called sashimi.

questions.question: What is the main herb in a traditional pesto?
questions.fact: Classic Genoese pesto is basil, pine nuts, garlic, olive oil and cheese, traditionally ground in a marble mortar.

questions.question: Which pasta's name means "little ears"?
questions.fact: Orecchiette are the classic pasta of Puglia, in the "heel" of Italy, often served with turnip tops.

questions.question: Farfalle pasta is shaped like…
questions.fact: "Farfalle" means "butterflies" in Italian.

questions.question: Which country is most famous for croissants?
questions.fact: The croissant probably came from an Austrian pastry, the kipferl, before Paris made it famous.

questions.question: What is falafel mainly made from?
questions.fact: Falafel is often made with chickpeas, but in Egypt it's usually made with fava beans.

questions.question: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
questions.fact: It takes about four kilos of fresh grapes to make one kilo of raisins.

questions.question: What are dried plums called?
questions.fact: Prunes are especially famous from Agen in France, where they've been grown for centuries.

questions.question: What is Japanese rice wine called?
questions.fact: Sake is brewed a bit like beer, from rice, water and a mould called koji, and is often served warm.

questions.question: Pad thai comes from which country?
questions.fact: Pad thai became a national dish in the 1930s and 40s, when the Thai government promoted it.

questions.question: Which cheese is used on a classic pizza Margherita?
questions.fact: Real Neapolitan pizza is cooked in a wood-fired oven at around 450 °C, for only about 90 seconds.

questions.question: Which nut is the main ingredient of Nutella?
questions.fact: Nutella was created in Italy after World War II, when cocoa was scarce, so hazelnuts were mixed in to stretch it.

questions.question: Champagne comes from which country?
questions.fact: Only sparkling wine from the Champagne region of France can be called champagne.

questions.question: What is Spain's best-known sparkling wine called?
questions.fact: Most cava is made in Catalonia, especially around Sant Sadurní d'Anoia in the Penedès.

questions.question: Which Italian sparkling wine comes from the Veneto region?
questions.fact: Prosecco is named after a village near Trieste, in north-east Italy.

questions.question: Which Spanish ham comes from black Iberian pigs?
questions.fact: The best jamón ibérico, "de bellota", comes from pigs that roam oak forests eating acorns.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of patatas bravas?
questions.fact: "Bravas" means fierce, after the spicy sauce. Many say they were invented in Madrid.

questions.question: Which Mexican dish is a folded tortilla filled with melted cheese?
questions.fact: "Queso" means cheese in Spanish, which is where the name quesadilla comes from.

questions.question: What is tofu made from?
questions.fact: Tofu is made a bit like cheese: soy milk is curdled and the curds are pressed into blocks.

questions.question: Which vegetable is used to make sauerkraut?
questions.fact: "Sauerkraut" means "sour cabbage" in German. Sailors took it on voyages to help prevent scurvy.

questions.question: Goulash is a famous dish from which country?
questions.fact: Goulash was first cooked by Hungarian cattle herders, and it gets its colour and flavour from paprika.

questions.question: Which spice gives curry its yellow colour?
questions.fact: Turmeric has been used for thousands of years in India, in food and as a dye.

questions.question: Pimentón, the paprika used in chorizo, is made from…
questions.fact: The most famous Spanish pimentón, from La Vera in Extremadura, is smoked over oak wood.

questions.question: What is meringue made of?
questions.fact: Meringue is said to be named after the Swiss town of Meiringen, though no one is completely sure.

questions.question: Crema catalana is very similar to which French dessert?
questions.fact: Crema catalana is traditionally eaten on 19 March, Saint Joseph's Day, and is also called "crema de Sant Josep".

questions.question: What kind of food is brie?
questions.fact: Brie comes from the region of the same name near Paris and is sometimes called "the queen of cheeses".

questions.question: Moussaka is most famously a dish from…
questions.fact: Greek moussaka has layers of aubergine, minced meat and a creamy béchamel topping.

questions.question: What are the small dishes served in Spanish bars called?
questions.fact: One popular story says tapas began as a slice of bread or ham placed on top of a glass to keep the flies out ("tapar" means to cover).

questions.question: Dim sum belongs to which cuisine?
questions.fact: Dim sum is traditionally eaten with tea at brunch in Cantonese "yum cha" restaurants.

questions.question: Which tropical fruit is famous for its very strong smell?
questions.fact: The durian smells so strong that it's banned on public transport and in many hotels in Singapore.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of an Italian risotto?
questions.fact: Risotto is made with short-grain rice like arborio, stirred slowly so it turns creamy.

questions.question: Couscous is made from which grain?
questions.fact: Couscous is the national dish of several North African countries, and UNESCO lists it as cultural heritage.

questions.question: What is the main spirit in a mojito?
questions.fact: The mojito comes from Cuba and is said to have been a favourite of writer Ernest Hemingway.

questions.question: Which spirit is a margarita based on?
questions.fact: Tequila can only be made from blue agave, mostly in the Mexican state of Jalisco.

questions.question: Sangria is traditionally made with…
questions.fact: Sangria comes from "sangre", Spanish for blood, because of its deep red colour.

questions.question: What is Valencian "horchata de chufa" made from?
questions.fact: Horchata is traditionally enjoyed in Valencia with "fartons", long sweet pastries for dipping.

questions.question: Which coffee is espresso topped with steamed milk and lots of foam?
questions.fact: The cappuccino is named after Capuchin friars, whose brown robes matched the drink's colour.

questions.question: In Spain, a "cortado" is espresso with…
questions.fact: "Cortado" means "cut": the espresso is cut with a little milk.

questions.question: Which country produces the most coffee in the world?
questions.fact: Brazil grows around a third of the world's coffee.

questions.question: Which country is the world's biggest producer of olive oil?
questions.fact: Spain produces more olive oil than any other country, most of it in Andalusia, especially the province of Jaén.

questions.question: Baba ganoush is made mainly from…
questions.fact: Baba ganoush is made by roasting aubergines until the skin chars, which gives it a smoky taste.

questions.question: What is ceviche?
options: Raw fish cured in citrus juice
questions.fact: Ceviche is Peru's national dish. The citrus juice "cooks" the fish without any heat.

questions.question: Pierogi dumplings are a classic dish of which country?
questions.fact: Pierogi can be filled with potato and cheese, meat, sauerkraut or even fruit.

questions.question: Kimchi is a famous fermented dish from…
questions.fact: There are hundreds of kinds of kimchi. Traditionally it was fermented in clay pots buried in the ground.

questions.question: What is inside a Portuguese "pastel de nata"?
questions.fact: Pastéis de nata were created by monks at a monastery in Belém, Lisbon, centuries ago.

questions.question: Turrón, the Spanish Christmas sweet, is mainly almonds and…
questions.fact: The two classic turrones are hard "Alicante" with whole almonds and soft "Jijona" with ground almonds.

questions.question: Fondue is a classic dish from…
questions.fact: Swiss tradition says that whoever drops their bread into the fondue has to pay a forfeit.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of Basque "bacalao al pil pil"?
questions.fact: "Pil pil" is the sound the sauce makes as the cod is gently shaken in hot oil and garlic.

questions.question: "Pulpo a la gallega" is made with…
questions.fact: Pulpo a la gallega is served on wooden plates with olive oil, salt and paprika.

questions.question: Classic marmalade is made from which fruit?
questions.fact: British marmalade is traditionally made with bitter Seville oranges from Spain.

questions.question: Which part of a chilli pepper is the hottest?
questions.fact: Capsaicin, the chemical that makes chillies hot, is concentrated in the white membrane, not in the seeds.

questions.question: Poutine (chips with cheese curds and gravy) comes from which country?
questions.fact: Poutine comes from Quebec in the 1950s. "Poutine" is slang for "a mess" in Quebec French.

questions.question: What is "cochinillo asado", the famous dish of Segovia?
questions.fact: Segovia's famous restaurant tradition is to cut the cochinillo with the edge of a plate to show how tender it is.

questions.question: Chocolate is made from which bean?
questions.fact: The Aztecs drank chocolate as a bitter drink and even used cocoa beans as money.

questions.question: Wasabi is usually served with…
questions.fact: Most "wasabi" outside Japan is actually horseradish with green colouring. Real wasabi is rare and expensive.

questions.question: Which herb goes into a classic mojito?
questions.fact: Rub the mint gently: crushing it too hard releases bitter flavours.

questions.question: Which sheep's cheese comes from La Mancha?
questions.fact: Manchego is made from the milk of Manchega sheep, and its rind has a zig-zag pattern from traditional grass moulds.

questions.question: Which dark beer style, like Guinness, uses roasted barley?
questions.fact: Guinness looks black, but held up to the light it's actually a very dark ruby red.

questions.question: How many teaspoons make one tablespoon?
questions.fact: Three teaspoons make a tablespoon, and 16 tablespoons make an American cup.
